name: Hadwiger conjecture
question: Does every graph of chromatic number k contain Kk as a minor?
first_attack: Audit precise statement and prove a restricted case
method_title: Replay the object, or mine the census
dispatch_next: Extract a concrete finite graph from the binary-frame construction, or obtain two independent specialist reviews of the existential proof; do not treat comparator or second-kernel replay as a finite witness.
dispatch_why: The extractability audit found no published finite Hadwiger graph. Extracting one, or obtaining specialist reviews of the existential proof, still outranks another small-n census. Robertson, Seymour and Thomas already cover chromatic number at most 6.

campaign.method: Colouring and minor-model certificates over exhaustive graph censuses
campaign.hypothesis: Every graph with chromatic number t has K_t as a minor.
campaign.first_proof_obligation: Choose a restricted class beyond the proved t <= 6 range (for example 7-chromatic graphs with small independence number) and state a checkable lemma absent from the literature.
campaign.next_experiment: Extend the census engine to 8-9 vertices with a faster canonical labeller, then target contraction-critical 7-chromatic graphs where a K7 minor model must be certified.
campaign.falsification: A graph with a certified chromatic-number lower bound t and an exhaustive certificate that no K_t minor model exists.
campaign.blocker: Every graph a naive census reaches is inside the proved t <= 6 range; t = 7 needs much larger graphs and exact chromatic lower-bound certificates.

probes.name: Hadwiger conjecture
probes.title: Hadwiger's conjecture on every graph up to N vertices
probes.frontier: Known: proved for chromatic number <= 6 (Robertson, Seymour & Thomas 1993), so every graph on <= 7 vertices is a known case. Reproduction only.

smoke.scope: Every graph on 1..6 vertices has a proper t-colouring and a K_t minor model for t = its chromatic number.

deep.scope: Every graph on 1..7 vertices has a proper t-colouring and a K_t minor model for t = its chromatic number.

milestones.title: Hadwiger's conjecture certified on all 208 graphs with at most 6 vertices
milestones.scope: Known case (chromatic number <= 6 theorem); not new
milestones.description: Each graph carries a proper t-colouring and a K_t minor model (t = chromatic number); the census is complete by Burnside counting. Deep run: all 1,252 graphs on <= 7 vertices.

claim_review_2026.claimed_theorem: Arbitrarily large finite simple graphs have fractional chromatic number chi_f(G) > h(G), where h is largest clique-minor order.
claim_review_2026.scope_note: Since chi(G)>=chi_f(G), such a graph would refute chi(G)<=h(G), the registered Hadwiger statement.
claim_review_2026.known_caveats: Comparator acceptance is proof-object checking only. The 2026-10-31 extractability audit (research/M071_M073_WITNESSES.md; data/claim_witness_replay.json) confirms the Lean statement is an existential family (arbitrarily large m, alpha<=2, h(G)<26m/75+2/3<m/2<=chi(G)) with no published adjacency list or explicit Hadwiger number. Bonnet's local kernel replay remains Lean-only evidence.
claim_review_2026.next_review: Extract a concrete finite graph from the binary-frame construction, or obtain two independent specialist reviews of the existential proof; do not treat comparator or second-kernel replay as a finite witness.

formal_statement.encodes: Every simple graph has a K_t minor (branch-set model, connectivity by no-split cuts) or a proper (t−1)-colouring.
